newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - API seen bearish as gas output hits record.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - API seen bearish as gas output hits record.

text.p: REUTER SURVEY ESTIMATES* ACTUAL STOCKS FOR
FOR WEEK ENDED 06/13/97 WEEK ENDED 06/13/97-CHANGE
DISTILLATE...... UP 2.500 112.542 UP 3.288 MLN

*NB - The survey estimate is derived by omitting the high and low forecast and averaging the rest, with a sample of at least six.
(STOCKS IN THOUSANDS/BBLS, CHANGES IN MLN/BBLS)
The American Petroleum Instutute (API) continued to paint a bearish picture of crude oil and petroleum products in the United States in its latest weekly status report on Tuesday.

Crude oil imports hit a record 9.4 million barrels per day (bpd) in the week ended June 13, up nearly a million bpd on the previous week. At the same time, gasoline output set a record 8.23 million bpd after breaking the record set two weeks prior.
Richard Redash, an energy markets analyst at Prudential Securities in New York, said the API report is bearish for the market.
"There was a neglible draw in crude and without (the volatile West Coast district) PADD 5 there would have been a 1.73 million barrel increase," said Redash.
"The API data is bearish for the whole complex," he added.

The market will want to see confirmation of the API's data in Wednesday morning's Department of Energy report, but the trend has been in place for several months, said Nizam Sharif, an analyst at Hornsby & Co, Inc in Houston.

While gasoline demand over the past month has been running at more than three percent above the same period in 1996, gasoline imports have also been on a rising trend, comprised mostly of the blending component methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE), used to oxygenate gasoline.

Combined with the exceptionally high production rate which has outstripped demand, gasoline stocks have been rising sharply in the past six weeks against the seasonal trend usually seen in the past six years and cutting the year-on-year stocks deficit to just over a million barrels.
Distillate stocks also have been soaring and rose another 3.3 million barrels last week, putting stocks more than 13 million barrels above last year's level at 112.5 million barrels.

But even while refinery runs have been running at or near record levels (down slightly last week), crude stocks have been rising sharply since the start of this year, reversing a long downtrend over the previous three years or so.
"Refiners are running flat out and they are going to continue running flat out and it is going to translate crude inventories into product inventories," said Sharif.

"If Iraqi barrels are not coming out for a few weeks it might have a little repreive but the picture is progressively getting worse and worse," said Sharif, referring to the hold up in restarting Iraq's "oil-for-food" deal as Baghdad works on a plan to try to ensure quicker processing of its humanitarian imports.
In ACCESS trading after hours on Tuesday (which was delayed due to technical problems), crude futures prices slid. July, which expires on Friday, was down 19 cents at $19.04 a barrel.
July heating oil was down 0.20 at 52.25 cents a gallon, while gasoline futures were down 0.68 at 57.80 cents a gallon.
-- New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1620
